target_moa.text: Umbralisib is a small molecule inhibitor of phosphoinositide-3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) and casein kinase 1 epsilon (CK1ε); it competitively binds PI3Kδ and CK1ε, inhibiting cell proliferation and inducing apoptosis of lymphoma and leukemic cells.

citations.quote: Umbralisib is a small molecule inhibitor of phosphoinositide-3-kinase delta (PI3Kδ) and casein kinase 1 epsilon (CK1ε). The mechanism of action (MOA) involves competitive binding of umbralisib to PI3Kδ and CK1ε, inhibiting cell proliferation and inducing apoptosis of lymphoma and leukemic cell lines and primary tumor cells.

key_safety.text: Most common (≥15%) adverse reactions including lab abnormalities were increased creatinine, diarrhea-colitis, fatigue, nausea, neutropenia, transaminase elevation, musculoskeletal pain, anemia, thrombocytopenia, upper respiratory tract infection, vomiting, abdominal pain, decreased appetite, and rash. Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 51.2% of the safety pool, most commonly neutropenia (11.3%), diarrhea/colitis (8.4%), and increased transaminases (6.5%). Primary safety issues include serious/fatal infections and cutaneous reactions, serious diarrhea or colitis, hepatotoxicity, and neutropenia.

citations.quote: The most common (\ge 15\%) adverse reactions, including laboratory abnormalities, were increased creatinine, diarrhea-colitis, fatigue, nausea, neutropenia, transaminase elevation, musculoskeletal pain, anemia, thrombocytopenia, upper respiratory tract infection, vomiting, abdominal pain, decreased appetite, and rash.

The incidence of Grade ≥3 adverse events was 51.2% and 59.4% in the safety pool and patients with MZL, respectively. The most common Grade ≥3 adverse events in the safety pool and in patients with MZL were neutropenia (11.3%, 13%), diarrhea/colitis (8.4%, 11.6%) and increased transaminases (6.5%, 11.6%), respectively.
The primary safety issues identified with umbralisib include serious, including fatal, infections and cutaneous reactions, and serious diarrhea or colitis, hepatotoxicity, and neutropenia.
